papers.title: CSK-DDI: Compensating Structural Incompleteness with Knowledge Graph World Knowledge for Drug–Drug Interaction Modeling
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction is critical for drug safety, yet existing methods suffer from structural incompleteness in drug representation. Motif and molecular graph encodings capture local substructures and global topology but remain confined to the closed structural space of individual molecules, lacking cross-entity and contextual information and leading to limited generalization, especially in cold-start scenarios. To address this issue, we propose CSK-DDI, a multimodal framework that jointly encodes motif-level chemical patterns, molecular graph topology, and biomedical knowledge graph context as complementary drug representations. The KG encodes drugs’ contextual positions and relational semantics through multi-entity and multi-relation connections, providing global cross-entity and cross-semantic information that complements structural representations. The resulting fusion captures local chemical patterns, global topology, and biomedical context in a unified embedding. Results CSK-DDI employs a cross-attention mechanism to enable multi-view interaction among motif, molecular graph, and knowledge graph representations, producing unified structure-aware and context-aware drug embeddings. To improve robustness under sparse conditions, the model further incorporates a cold-start-oriented representation enhancement strategy. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, with particularly notable gains in cold-start scenarios. Availability Source code and data are available at https://github.com/cgwcbz2/CSK-DDI and on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21415769

MOTIVATION: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction is critical for drug safety, yet existing methods suffer from structural incompleteness in drug representation. Motif and molecular graph encodings capture local substructures and global topology but remain confined to the closed structural space of individual molecules, lacking cross-entity and contextual information and leading to limited generalization, especially in cold-start scenarios. To address this issue, we propose CSK-DDI, a multimodal framework that jointly encodes motif-level chemical patterns, molecular graph topology, and biomedical knowledge graph context as complementary drug representations. The KG encodes drugs' contextual positions and relational semantics through multi-entity and multi-relation connections, providing global cross-entity and cross-semantic information that complements structural representations. The resulting fusion captures local chemical patterns, global topology, and biomedical context in a unified embedding.

RESULTS: CSK-DDI employs a cross-attention mechanism to enable multi-view interaction among motif, molecular graph, and knowledge graph representations, producing unified structure-aware and context-aware drug embeddings. To improve robustness under sparse conditions, the model further incorporates a cold-start-oriented representation enhancement strategy. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, with particularly notable gains in cold-start scenarios.

AVAILABILITY: Source code and data are available at https://github.com/cgwcbz2/CSK-DDI and on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21415769.

为了解决这个问题，我们提出了 CSK-DDI，这是一个多模式框架，它联合编码基序级化学模式、分子图拓扑和生物医学知识图上下文作为补充药物表示。
KG通过多实体和多关系连接对药物的上下文位置和关系语义进行编码，提供补充结构表示的全局跨实体和跨语义信息。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 药物相互作用（DDI）预测对于药物安全至关重要，但现有方法在药物表征方面存在结构不完整的问题。基序和分子图编码捕获局部子结构和全局拓扑，但仍然局限于单个分子的封闭结构空间，缺乏跨实体和上下文信息，导致泛化能力有限，特别是在冷启动场景中。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了 CSK-DDI，这是一个多模式框架，它联合编码基序级化学模式、分子图拓扑和生物医学知识图上下文作为补充药物表示。 KG通过多实体和多关系连接对药物的上下文位置和关系语义进行编码，提供补充结构表示的全局跨实体和跨语义信息。由此产生的融合在统一的嵌入中捕获局部化学模式、全局拓扑和生物医学背景。结果 CSK-DDI 采用交叉注意机制来实现主题、分子图和知识图表示之间的多视图交互，从而产生统一的结构感知和上下文感知药物嵌入。为了提高稀疏条件下的鲁棒性，该模型进一步结合了面向冷启动的表示增强策略。对基准数据集的实验表明，与最先进的方法相比，取得了一致的改进，尤其是在冷启动场景中取得了显着的进步。可用性 源代码和数据可在 https://github.com/cgwcbz2/CSK-DDI 和 Zenodo 上获取：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21415769

papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction is critical for drug safety, yet existing methods suffer from structural incompleteness in drug representation. Motif and molecular graph encodings capture local substructures and global topology but remain confined to the closed structural space of individual molecules, lacking cross-entity and contextual information and leading to limited generalization, especially in cold-start scenarios. To address this issue, we propose CSK-DDI, a multimodal framework that jointly encodes motif-level chemical patterns, molecular graph topology, and biomedical knowledge graph context as complementary drug representations. The KG encodes drugs' contextual positions and relational semantics through multi-entity and multi-relation connections, providing global cross-entity and cross-semantic information that complements structural representations. The resulting fusion captures local chemical patterns, global topology, and biomedical context in a unified embedding.

RESULTS: CSK-DDI employs a cross-attention mechanism to enable multi-view interaction among motif, molecular graph, and knowledge graph representations, producing unified structure-aware and context-aware drug embeddings. To improve robustness under sparse conditions, the model further incorporates a cold-start-oriented representation enhancement strategy. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, with particularly notable gains in cold-start scenarios.

AVAILABILITY: Source code and data are available at https://github.com/cgwcbz2/CSK-DDI and on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21415769.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
